namespace OAI.Algorithms

/-!
# Canonical truncation before substitution

Polynomials are represented with U outermost, Z in the middle, and the X variables
innermost.  Truncation is an operation on canonical polynomial representatives;
we never assert that U = 1 defines a map out of the truncated quotient.
-/

namespace SubexponentialSAT.Truncation

noncomputable section

open scoped BigOperators

variable {R ι : Type*} [CommSemiring R]

abbrev Poly (ι R : Type*) [CommSemiring R] :=
  Polynomial (Polynomial (MvPolynomial ι R))

/-- Delete all coefficients of degree at least n. -/
def trunc {A : Type*} [Semiring A] (n : ℕ) (P : Polynomial A) : Polynomial A :=
  Polynomial.ofFinsupp (.ofCoeff (P.toFinsupp.coeff.filter fun j => j < n))

@[simp] theorem coeff_trunc {A : Type*} [Semiring A]
    (n j : ℕ) (P : Polynomial A) :
    (trunc n P).coeff j = if j < n then P.coeff j else 0 := by
  classical
  simp [trunc, Polynomial.coeff, Finsupp.filter_apply]

@[simp] theorem trunc_zero {A : Type*} [Semiring A] (n : ℕ) :
    trunc n (0 : Polynomial A) = 0 := by
  ext j
  simp

    (n : ℕ) (P Q : Polynomial A) :
    trunc n (P + Q) = trunc n P + trunc n Q := by
  ext j
  by_cases h : j < n <;> simp [h]

/-- Delete X monomials whose total degree exceeds N. -/
def xTrunc (N : ℕ) (P : MvPolynomial ι R) : MvPolynomial ι R :=
  .ofCoeff ((AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff P).filter
    fun a : ι →₀ ℕ => a.sum (fun _ k => k) ≤ N)

    (xTrunc N P).coeff a =
      if a.sum (fun _ k => k) ≤ N then P.coeff a else 0 := by
  classical
  simp [xTrunc, Finsupp.filter_apply]

@[simp] theorem xTrunc_zero (N : ℕ) : xTrunc N (0 : MvPolynomial ι R) = 0 := by
  ext a
  simp

/-!
# MODULE: quantized_layer_composition
SOURCES: src/core/layer.cpp
The GDN / QSA / MoE layer composition: Q8_K/Q8_0 activation sizing, the three-plane layout check of a
quantized weight (`plane_ptrs`), the per-tensor activation dispatch (`gemv_quantized`), the 16-byte
aligned arena carving (`gdn_buffers_init`, `Cursor`), and the stage-selection logic of `block_layer_pre`.

## Source semantics
* A Q8_K image of `n` floats is `n/256` blocks of 292 bytes; a Q8_0 image is `n/32` blocks of 34 bytes.
* A quantized tensor is codes ++ scales ++ offsets; the three sizes recorded by the loader must add up to
  the tensor, codes and scales are non-empty, and `has_offset` iff the offset plane is non-empty.
* The activation a quantized weight wants is a property of the TENSOR: S2 (`code_bits = 2`) wants Q8_0;
  any other form wants Q8_K iff its manifest `source_type` says so (`wants_q8k`), otherwise Q8_0.
* Every scratch region is carved at a 16-byte aligned offset; the carve's total is the sum of the
  aligned parts and is never smaller than the raw sum.
* `block_layer_pre` runs stage k (0..4) when `stage_prefix > k` if a prefix is given, otherwise by
  `half` (0 = all; 1 = mixer stages 0..2; 2 = FFN-front stages 3..4).
* The MoE `k` must lie in 1..64.

## Form template identifiers
q8kBytes ↔ q8k_bytes · q8_0Bytes ↔ `(n/32)*34` · WeightRef/PlanesOk ↔ WeightRef + plane_ptrs ·
wantedAct ↔ gemv_quantized dispatch · align16/carve/carveTotal ↔ Cursor::take / gdn_buffers_init ·
runStage ↔ run0..run4 · kValid ↔ `k < 1 || k > 64` guard
-/

namespace QuantizedLayerComposition

-- § activation image sizes

/-- Bytes of a Q8_K activation image (`q8k_bytes`). -/
def q8kBytes (n : Nat) : Nat := (n / 256) * 292

/-- Bytes of a Q8_0 activation image. -/
def q8_0Bytes (n : Nat) : Nat := (n / 32) * 34

/-- A whole number of 256-blocks has exactly 292 bytes per block. -/
theorem q8kBytes_blocks (b : Nat) : q8kBytes (256 * b) = 292 * b := by
  unfold q8kBytes
  rw [Nat.mul_div_cancel_left b (by decide)]
  exact Nat.mul_comm b 292

/-- A whole number of 32-blocks has exactly 34 bytes per block. -/
theorem q8_0Bytes_blocks (b : Nat) : q8_0Bytes (32 * b) = 34 * b := by
  unfold q8_0Bytes
  rw [Nat.mul_div_cancel_left b (by decide)]
  exact Nat.mul_comm b 34

/-- The model width 2560 gives the concrete Q8_K/Q8_0 sizes used by every layer buffer. -/
theorem n_embd_images : q8kBytes 2560 = 2920 ∧ q8_0Bytes 2560 = 2720 := by
  decide

-- § the three planes of a quantized tensor

/-- The fields of a `WeightRef` the plane check reads. -/
structure WeightRef where
  codeBits : Nat
  codesBytes : Nat
  scalesBytes : Nat
  offsetBytes : Nat
  bytes : Nat
  hasOffset : Bool

/-- What `plane_ptrs` accepts: an S2/S4/S8 width, non-empty codes and scales, planes that add up to the
tensor, and `has_offset` agreeing with the offset plane. -/
structure PlanesOk (r : WeightRef) : Prop where
  width : r.codeBits = 2 ∨ r.codeBits = 4 ∨ r.codeBits = 8
  codes_pos : 0 < r.codesBytes
  scales_pos : 0 < r.scalesBytes
  sum : r.codesBytes + r.scalesBytes + r.offsetBytes = r.bytes
  offset_flag : (r.hasOffset = true) ↔ r.offsetBytes ≠ 0

/-- Byte offset of the scale plane. -/
def scalesStart (r : WeightRef) : Nat := r.codesBytes

/-- Byte offset of the offset plane. -/
def offsetStart (r : WeightRef) : Nat := r.codesBytes + r.scalesBytes

/-- The scale plane begins strictly inside the tensor and after the codes. -/
theorem scales_inside (r : WeightRef) (h : PlanesOk r) : scalesStart r < r.bytes := by
  have hs := h.sum
  have hp := h.scales_pos
  unfold scalesStart
  omega

/-- The offset plane ends exactly at the end of the tensor: nothing is read past it. -/
theorem offset_ends_at_tensor_end (r : WeightRef) (h : PlanesOk r) :
    offsetStart r + r.offsetBytes = r.bytes := by
  unfold offsetStart
  exact h.sum

/-- The three planes are disjoint and ordered: codes, then scales, then offsets. -/
theorem planes_ordered (r : WeightRef) (h : PlanesOk r) :
    r.codesBytes ≤ scalesStart r ∧ scalesStart r + r.scalesBytes = offsetStart r ∧
      offsetStart r ≤ r.bytes := by
  have hs := h.sum
  refine ⟨Nat.le_refl _, rfl, ?_⟩
  unfold offsetStart
  omega

/-- A tensor without the offset flag has an empty offset plane, so codes and scales fill it. -/
theorem no_offset_two_planes (r : WeightRef) (h : PlanesOk r) (hf : r.hasOffset = false) :
    r.codesBytes + r.scalesBytes = r.bytes := by
  have hz : r.offsetBytes = 0 := by
    cases hb : decide (r.offsetBytes = 0) with
    | true => exact of_decide_eq_true hb
    | false =>
      have hne : r.offsetBytes ≠ 0 := of_decide_eq_false hb
      have := h.offset_flag.mpr hne
      rw [hf] at this
      exact absurd this (by decide)
  have hs := h.sum
  omega

-- § activation dispatch

/-- The two canonical quantized activation formats. -/
inductive ActKind where
  | q8_0
  | q8_K
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Which activation image a quantized weight consumes (`gemv_quantized`). -/
def wantedAct (codeBits : Nat) (wantsQ8K : Bool) : ActKind :=
  if codeBits = 2 then .q8_0 else if wantsQ8K then .q8_K else .q8_0

/-- An S2 tensor always takes Q8_0, whatever its manifest says. -/
theorem s2_takes_q8_0 (w : Bool) : wantedAct 2 w = .q8_0 := by
  simp [wantedAct]

/-- A non-S2 K-quant takes Q8_K. -/
theorem kquant_takes_q8K (c : Nat) (h : c ≠ 2) : wantedAct c true = .q8_K := by
  simp [wantedAct, h]

/-- A legacy form (Q4_0/Q5_0/Q8_0/IQ4_NL) takes Q8_0 regardless of its width: the width cannot decide. -/
theorem legacy_takes_q8_0 (c : Nat) : wantedAct c false = .q8_0 := by
  by_cases h : c = 2 <;> simp [wantedAct, h]

/-- Two tensors of the same width can still want different activations: `code_bits` alone is not the rule. -/
theorem width_does_not_decide : wantedAct 4 true ≠ wantedAct 4 false := by
  decide

-- § 16-byte aligned carving

/-- Round up to a multiple of 16 (`(v + 15) & ~15`). -/
def align16 (n : Nat) : Nat := (n + 15) / 16 * 16

/-- Rounding up never shrinks a region. -/
theorem align16_ge (n : Nat) : n ≤ align16 n := by
  unfold align16; omega

/-- The rounded size is a multiple of 16. -/
theorem align16_mod (n : Nat) : align16 n % 16 = 0 := by
  unfold align16; omega

/-- Rounding up wastes fewer than 16 bytes. -/
theorem align16_lt (n : Nat) : align16 n < n + 16 := by
  unfold align16; omega

/-- The start offsets the carve assigns to `parts`, beginning at `at`. -/
def carve : List Nat → Nat → List Nat
  | [], _ => []
  | p :: ps, at => at :: carve ps (at + align16 p)

/-- The bytes the carve consumes. -/
def carveTotal : List Nat → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | p :: ps => align16 p + carveTotal ps

/-- The raw byte sum of the parts. -/
def rawSum : List Nat → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | p :: ps => p + rawSum ps

/-- One offset per part. -/
theorem carve_length : ∀ (ps : List Nat) (a : Nat), (carve ps a).length = ps.length
  | [], _ => rfl
  | _ :: ps, a => by
    simp only [carve, List.length_cons]
    rw [carve_length ps]

/-- From an aligned base, every carved offset is 16-byte aligned. -/
theorem carve_aligned :
    ∀ (ps : List Nat) (a : Nat), a % 16 = 0 → ∀ x ∈ carve ps a, x % 16 = 0
  | [], _, _, x, hx => by simp [carve] at hx
  | p :: ps, a, ha, x, hx => by
    simp only [carve, List.mem_cons] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | hx
    · exact ha
    · have hp := align16_mod p
      exact carve_aligned ps (a + align16 p) (by omega) x hx

/-- Every carved offset lies inside `[a, a + total]`: the arena of `carveTotal` bytes holds them all. -/
theorem carve_in_arena :
    ∀ (ps : List Nat) (a : Nat), ∀ x ∈ carve ps a, a ≤ x ∧ x ≤ a + carveTotal ps
  | [], _, x, hx => by simp [carve] at hx
  | p :: ps, a, x, hx => by
    simp only [carve, List.mem_cons] at hx
    simp only [carveTotal]
    rcases hx with rfl | hx
    · omega
    · have ih := carve_in_arena ps (a + align16 p) x hx
      omega

/-- The aligned total covers the raw sum of the parts (`gdn_buffers_bytes` is an upper bound). -/
theorem carveTotal_ge_rawSum : ∀ ps : List Nat, rawSum ps ≤ carveTotal ps

  unfold kValid at h; omega

end QuantizedLayerComposition

/-!
# MODULE: session_token_pipeline
SOURCES: src/core/session.cpp
One token through all 48 layers: the session arena sizing, the per-layer GDN state slices
(`gdn_point_at`), the QSA/GDN layer interleave, the doorbell sequence the host loop waits on
(`session_loop`, `session_run_token`), and the prefix-differencing stage table
(`session_replay_stage_prefixes`).

## Source semantics
* Layer `l` is QSA iff `l % 4 = 3`; the remaining layers are GDN.  Each GDN layer owns its own
  recurrent + conv state slice at `gdn_index * gdn_state_floats`; slices of distinct GDN layers are
  disjoint, which is what keeps one layer's recurrence from leaking into the next.
* `gdn_index(l)` counts the GDN layers strictly before `l`; with `qsa_index` it partitions `l`.
* The arena is `align_up(n, 256) + 4096` and therefore covers the raw sum `n`.
* The host waits for `seq ≥ l + 1` at layer `l`; the ring is monotone, so the l-th wait is satisfied by
  the l-th ring and the token completes after exactly `n_layers` rings.
* The five-stage table is built from cumulative prefix times t1..t5; the differences telescope back to
  t5, which is the check the source prints ("the five must account for it").

## Form template identifiers
isQsa ↔ is_qsa_layer · gdnIndex/qsaIndex ↔ gdn_point_at / qsa_index · sliceStart ↔ s.gdn_state + i*F ·
alignUp ↔ align_up · sessionArena ↔ session_bytes · ringSatisfied ↔ `*seq >= want` · stageDiffs ↔ t[0..4]
-/

namespace SessionTokenPipeline

-- § layer kinds

/-- `full_attention_interval = 4`: every fourth layer, index 3 mod 4, is a QSA layer. -/
def isQsa (l : Nat) : Bool := l % 4 == 3

/-- The number of GDN layers strictly before `l` (the slice index `gdn_point_at` computes). -/
def gdnIndex : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | l + 1 => gdnIndex l + (if isQsa l then 0 else 1)

/-- The number of QSA layers strictly before `l` (the `qsa_index` counter of the capture loop). -/
def qsaIndex : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | l + 1 => qsaIndex l + (if isQsa l then 1 else 0)

/-- Every layer before `l` is counted exactly once, as GDN or as QSA. -/
theorem index_partition (l : Nat) : gdnIndex l + qsaIndex l = l := by
  induction l with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ n ih =>
    simp only [gdnIndex, qsaIndex]
    by_cases h : isQsa n = true <;> simp [h] <;> omega

/-- The artifact's 48 layers split into 36 GDN and 12 QSA layers. -/
theorem artifact_split : gdnIndex 48 = 36 ∧ qsaIndex 48 = 12 := by
  decide

/-- The GDN index is monotone: a later layer never gets an earlier slice. -/
theorem gdnIndex_mono (l : Nat) : gdnIndex l ≤ gdnIndex (l + 1) := by
  simp only [gdnIndex]
  omega

/-- Two distinct GDN layers get distinct slice indices: the index strictly grows past a GDN layer. -/
theorem gdnIndex_step (l : Nat) (h : isQsa l = false) : gdnIndex (l + 1) = gdnIndex l + 1 := by
  simp [gdnIndex, h]

/-- The GDN index never exceeds the layer index. -/
theorem gdnIndex_le (l : Nat) : gdnIndex l ≤ l := by
  have := index_partition l
  omega

-- § per-layer state slices

/-- Start of GDN slice `i` in floats. -/
def sliceStart (F i : Nat) : Nat := i * F

/-- Slices of distinct GDN indices are disjoint: slice `i` ends before slice `j` starts. -/
theorem slice_disjoint (F i j : Nat) (h : i < j) : sliceStart F i + F ≤ sliceStart F j := by
  unfold sliceStart
  have h1 : (i + 1) * F ≤ j * F := Nat.mul_le_mul_right F h
  rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul] at h1
  exact h1

/-- The last GDN slice ends inside the `n_gdn * F` floats `session_init` carves. -/
theorem slice_in_carve (F i n : Nat) (h : i < n) : sliceStart F i + F ≤ n * F := by
  have := slice_disjoint F i n h
  unfold sliceStart at this
  exact this

/-!
# MODULE: weight_pack_loader
SOURCES: src/core/weights.cpp
The dense-weight loader: each index row becomes a segment list (codes / scales / offsets for a
quantized tensor, one run otherwise), each segment carries a width transform (copy, bf16 high half,
f32→f16, fp16→f32 widening), and the segments are checked against the row's recorded totals before a
single byte moves.  A skip set compacts the arena by re-placing kept rows at the index alignment.

## Source semantics
* Quantized rows: codes (copy), scales (widened 2→4 B/elem iff `scales_fp16`), offsets (copy).  The
  destination planes are contiguous in the order codes, scales, offsets.
* A promoted row is exactly 4 B/elem in and 2 B/elem out; `Bf16High` keeps the top 16 bits of the
  f32 image, which is the bf16 encoding exactly, and loses only the low half.
* A widening chunk never splits an fp16 element: an odd tail is shortened by one.
* The staging output buffer is twice the input chunk because widening doubles the byte count.
* Compaction re-places kept rows at multiples of the alignment, so no two kept rows overlap.

## Form template identifiers
Seg/quantSegs ↔ Seg segs[3] · srcScaleBytes ↔ `scales_bytes / 2` · bf16High ↔ `v >> 16` ·
chunkLen ↔ the `n -= 1` tail rule · widenOut ↔ `elems * 4` · place ↔ the skip-set placement loop
-/

namespace WeightPackLoader

-- § the segment list of a quantized row

/-- One contiguous run of a row: source bytes in, destination bytes out, at a destination offset. -/
structure Seg where
  srcBytes : Nat
  dstOff : Nat
  dstBytes : Nat

/-- Source bytes of the scale plane: half the arena bytes when the pack holds fp16 scales. -/
def srcScaleBytes (scales : Nat) (fp16 : Bool) : Nat := if fp16 then scales / 2 else scales

/-- The three segments `load` builds for a quantized row. -/
def quantSegs (codes scales offs : Nat) (fp16 : Bool) : List Seg :=
  [⟨codes, 0, codes⟩, ⟨srcScaleBytes scales fp16, codes, scales⟩, ⟨offs, codes + scales, offs⟩]

/-- Sum of destination bytes. -/
def dstSum : List Seg → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | s :: ss => s.dstBytes + dstSum ss

/-- Sum of source bytes. -/
def srcSum : List Seg → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | s :: ss => s.srcBytes + srcSum ss

/-- The destination planes add up to codes + scales + offsets, the `dst_bytes` the index records. -/
theorem quant_dst_sum (c s o : Nat) (f : Bool) : dstSum (quantSegs c s o f) = c + s + o := by
  simp only [quantSegs, dstSum]
  omega

/-- Without fp16 scales the source span equals the destination span. -/
theorem quant_src_sum_f32 (c s o : Nat) : srcSum (quantSegs c s o false) = c + s + o := by
  simp only [quantSegs, srcSum, srcScaleBytes]
  omega

/-- With fp16 scales of an even byte count the source span is smaller by exactly half the scale plane. -/
theorem quant_src_sum_f16 (c s o : Nat) (he : s % 2 = 0) :
    srcSum (quantSegs c s o true) + s / 2 = c + s + o := by
  simp only [quantSegs, srcSum, srcScaleBytes, if_true]
  omega

/-- The destination planes are contiguous: each segment starts where the previous one ends. -/
theorem quant_dst_contiguous (c s o : Nat) (f : Bool) :
    match quantSegs c s o f with
    | [a, b, d] => a.dstOff + a.dstBytes = b.dstOff ∧ b.dstOff + b.dstBytes = d.dstOff
    | _ => False := by
  simp [quantSegs]

/-- The bf16 image of an f32 bit pattern: its high 16 bits. -/
def bf16High (v : Nat) : Nat := v / 65536

/-- The high half and the discarded low half reassemble the f32 bits exactly: nothing but the low

theorem bf16High_recombine (v : Nat) : bf16High v * 65536 + v % 65536 = v := by
  unfold bf16High; omega

/-- A promoted bf16 value (low half zero) is recovered exactly. -/
theorem bf16High_exact (v : Nat) (h : v % 65536 = 0) : bf16High v * 65536 = v := by
  have := bf16High_recombine v
  omega

/-- The high half of a 32-bit pattern fits in 16 bits. -/
theorem bf16High_fits (v : Nat) (h : v < 4294967296) : bf16High v < 65536 := by
  unfold bf16High; omega

/-- A promoted tensor of `e` elements: 4 bytes per element in, 2 out. -/
theorem promoted_halves (e : Nat) : (e * 4) / 4 * 2 = e * 2 := by
  omega

/-- Widening an even fp16 chunk of `n` bytes yields `2n` f32 bytes, which is why the output stage is
twice the input chunk. -/
theorem widen_doubles (n : Nat) (h : n % 2 = 0) : n / 2 * 4 = 2 * n := by
  omega

/-- Output never exceeds the `2 * CHUNK` staging buffer for any chunk of at most `CHUNK` bytes. -/
theorem widen_fits_stage (n chunk : Nat) (hn : n ≤ chunk) : n / 2 * 4 ≤ 2 * chunk := by
  omega

-- § chunking a widening plane

/-- The next chunk length: at most `chunk` and the remainder; shortened by one if odd. -/
def chunkLen (chunk rem : Nat) : Nat :=
  let n := min chunk rem
  if n % 2 = 1 then n - 1 else n

/-- A widening chunk is always a whole number of fp16 elements. -/
theorem chunkLen_even (chunk rem : Nat) : chunkLen chunk rem % 2 = 0 := by
  unfold chunkLen
  simp only
  split <;> omega

/-- A chunk never reads past the remaining plane. -/
theorem chunkLen_le_rem (chunk rem : Nat) : chunkLen chunk rem ≤ rem := by
  unfold chunkLen
  simp only
  split <;> omega

theorem chunkLen_progress (chunk rem : Nat) (hc : 2 ≤ chunk) (hr : 2 ≤ rem) :
    0 < chunkLen chunk rem := by
  unfold chunkLen
  simp only
  split <;> omega

/-- The 8 MiB chunk is even, so a full chunk is never shortened. -/
theorem full_chunk_unshortened (rem : Nat) (h : 8388608 ≤ rem) : chunkLen 8388608 rem = 8388608 := by
  unfold chunkLen
  simp only
  have hm : min 8388608 rem = 8388608 := Nat.min_eq_left h
  rw [hm]
  rfl

-- § compaction under a skip set

/-- Round up to the index alignment of 256 bytes. -/
def alignUp (n : Nat) : Nat := (n + 255) / 256 * 256

/-- Destination offsets of the kept rows, placed in index order from `base`. -/
def place : List Nat → Nat → List Nat
  | [], _ => []
  | b :: bs, base => base :: place bs (base + alignUp b)

/-- The pool the compacted arena needs. -/
def pool : List Nat → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | b :: bs => alignUp b + pool bs

/-- A row's bytes end before the next row's start: `alignUp` never shrinks. -/
theorem alignUp_ge (n : Nat) : n ≤ alignUp n := by
  unfold alignUp; omega

/-- Every placed row starts at an aligned offset when the base is aligned. -/
theorem place_aligned :
    ∀ (bs : List Nat) (a : Nat), a % 256 = 0 → ∀ x ∈ place bs a, x % 256 = 0
  | [], _, _, x, hx => by simp [place] at hx
  | b :: bs, a, ha, x, hx => by
    simp only [place, List.mem_cons] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | hx
    · exact ha
    · have hb : alignUp b % 256 = 0 := by unfold alignUp; omega
      exact place_aligned bs (a + alignUp b) (by omega) x hx

/-- Every placed row lies inside the pool: `[a, a + pool]` holds all offsets. -/
theorem place_in_pool :
    ∀ (bs : List Nat) (a : Nat), ∀ x ∈ place bs a, a ≤ x ∧ x ≤ a + pool bs
  | [], _, x, hx => by simp [place] at hx
  | b :: bs, a, x, hx => by
    simp only [place, List.mem_cons] at hx
    simp only [pool]
    rcases hx with rfl | hx
    · omega
    · have ih := place_in_pool bs (a + alignUp b) x hx
      omega

/-- The load refuses unless the arena holds the pool. -/
def arenaFits (arena need : Nat) : Prop := need ≤ arena

/-- A fitting arena holds every placed row's start. -/
theorem fits_holds_rows (arena : Nat) (bs : List Nat) (h : arenaFits arena (pool bs)) :
    ∀ x ∈ place bs 0, x ≤ arena := by
  intro x hx
  have := place_in_pool bs 0 x hx
  unfold arenaFits at h
  omega

end WeightPackLoader

/-!
# MODULE: native_dense_override
SOURCES: src/core/native_dense.cpp

payload bound, non-overlap with the next tensor), every eligible matrix must match its canonical shape,
and only when ALL checks and allocations succeed are the references published, sharing one Q8_1 scratch
sized for the widest input.

* A tensor's byte count is `(elements / block_elements) * block_bytes`; `elements` is the product of the
  dimensions, each multiplication guarded by `elements ≤ MAX / dim`.

  tensor (by sorted offset) iff `bytes ≤ next - offset`.

* The shared scratch is sized for the maximum `ne0` over the published matrices, so every projection's
  input fits.

extentOk ↔ `elements > MAX / dimension` guard · spanOk ↔ truncated-payload check ·
noOverlap ↔ `bytes > *next - offset` check · publishAll ↔ the final publish loop ·
maxIn ↔ max_in · shapeMatch ↔ incompatible-matrix check

/-- The multiplication guard: if `e ≤ M / d` then `e * d` does not exceed `M`. -/
theorem guarded_mul_le (e d M : Nat) (hd : 0 < d) (h : e ≤ M / d) : e * d ≤ M :=
  (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le hd).mp h

def extent (M : Nat) : List Nat → Option Nat
  | [] => some 1

    | none => none

/-- A guarded extent never exceeds the bound, for any bound at least 1. -/
theorem extent_le (M : Nat) (hM : 1 ≤ M) : ∀ (ds : List Nat) (e : Nat), extent M ds = some e → e ≤ M
  | [], e, h => by
    simp only [extent, Option.some.injEq] at h
    omega
  | d :: ds, e, h => by
    simp only [extent] at h
    split at h
    · exact absurd h (by simp)
    · rename_i e' _

      · simp [hd] at h
      · by_cases hg : e' ≤ M / d
        · simp only [hd, hg, if_false, if_true, Option.some.injEq] at h

        · simp [hd, hg] at h

theorem extent_zero_dim (M : Nat) (ds : List Nat) : extent M (0 :: ds) = none := by
  simp only [extent]
  split <;> simp

/-- Bytes of a tensor of `elements` elements stored in blocks. -/
def tensorBytes (elements blockElems blockBytes : Nat) : Nat := elements / blockElems * blockBytes

theorem blocks_exact (rows blocksPerRow blockElems blockBytes : Nat) (hb : 0 < blockElems) :

  unfold tensorBytes
  rw [← Nat.mul_assoc, Nat.mul_div_cancel _ hb]

def spanOk (offset bytes payload : Nat) : Prop := offset ≤ payload ∧ bytes ≤ payload - offset

  omega

theorem shapeMatch_int_safe (s0 s1 ne0 ne1 : Nat) (h : shapeMatch s0 s1 ne0 ne1) :
    0 < s0 ∧ s0 < 2147483648 ∧ 0 < s1 ∧ s1 < 2147483648 := by
  unfold shapeMatch at h; omega

    simpa using this
  · exact absurd rfl h

    (h : false ∈ checks) : publishAll checks pending = [] := by
  unfold publishAll
  have : checks.all id = false := by
    cases hc : checks.all id with
    | false => rfl
    | true =>
      have := List.all_eq_true.mp hc false h
      simp at this
  simp [this]

def maxIn : List Nat → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | x :: xs => max x (maxIn xs)

theorem input_fits_scratch : ∀ (xs : List Nat), ∀ x ∈ xs, x ≤ maxIn xs
  | [], x, hx => by simp at hx
  | y :: ys, x, hx => by
    simp only [List.mem_cons] at hx
    simp only [maxIn]
    rcases hx with rfl | hx
    · omega
    · have := input_fits_scratch ys x hx
      omega

end NativeDenseOverride

/-!
# MODULE: mtp_draft_layer
SOURCES: src/core/mtp.cpp
The multi-token-prediction draft layer: one attention + MoE block with its own K/V cache, captured as a
prefill graph (K/V only), a round graph (catch-up K/V for the window plus one full row) and one graph per
chain step.  The host stages step rows `[cell, cell+1, (cell+1)/4, cell+1]` and positions; the chain stops
as soon as a draft's probability falls below `min_p`.

## Source semantics
* The device arena is carved by a bump allocator rounding every region up to 256 bytes.
* Step rows: rows `0..T-1` are the catch-up window, rows `max_t + j - 1` (j = 1..max_t-2) the chain steps,
  and row `2*max_t - 1` the round's full row; these three groups never collide and all fit the
  `2 * max_t` rows allocated.
* The attention width `cap` is the window (or the context) rounded up to a multiple of 64; the window is
  used only when `0 < window < max_cells`.
* The chain emits 1 + (the number of leading steps whose previous probability passed `min_p`) drafts,
  never more than `max_t - 1`; unused draft slots are zeroed.
* `prefill` skips chunks the window can never reach again (`cell0 + c + T ≤ first_needed`).

## Form template identifiers
bumpTake ↔ Bump::take · stepRow ↔ put()/h_step_ fill · catchupRow/chainRow/fullRow ↔ t, max_t+j-1,
2*max_t-1 · capOf ↔ cap_ · windowOf ↔ window_ · chainLen ↔ the `pj >= min_p` loop
-/

namespace MtpDraftLayer

-- § the bump allocator

/-- Bytes a region of `n` bytes consumes from the bump arena. -/
def bumpTake (n : Nat) : Nat := (n + 255) / 256 * 256

/-- Region offsets of a sequence of requests, starting from `used`. -/
def bumpOffsets : List Nat → Nat → List Nat
  | [], _ => []
  | n :: ns, used => used :: bumpOffsets ns (used + bumpTake n)

/-- Final `used` after a sequence of requests (the counted pass, `count.used`). -/
def bumpUsed : List Nat → Nat → Nat
  | [], used => used
  | n :: ns, used => bumpUsed ns (used + bumpTake n)

/-- Every region is at least as large as requested. -/
theorem bumpTake_ge (n : Nat) : n ≤ bumpTake n := by
  unfold bumpTake; omega

/-- Every region is a multiple of 256 bytes. -/
theorem bumpTake_mod (n : Nat) : bumpTake n % 256 = 0 := by
  unfold bumpTake; omega

/-- All offsets are 256-aligned when the arena base is. -/
theorem offsets_aligned :
    ∀ (ns : List Nat) (u : Nat), u % 256 = 0 → ∀ x ∈ bumpOffsets ns u, x % 256 = 0
  | [], _, _, x, hx => by simp [bumpOffsets] at hx
  | n :: ns, u, hu, x, hx => by
    simp only [bumpOffsets, List.mem_cons] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | hx
    · exact hu
    · have := bumpTake_mod n
      exact offsets_aligned ns (u + bumpTake n) (by omega) x hx

/-- Every region of the real carve ends inside the arena sized by the counted carve: the two passes
walk the same sequence, so `cudaMalloc(count.used)` holds them all. -/
theorem regions_in_arena :
    ∀ (ns : List Nat) (u : Nat), ∀ x ∈ bumpOffsets ns u, u ≤ x ∧ x ≤ bumpUsed ns u
  | [], _, x, hx => by simp [bumpOffsets] at hx
  | n :: ns, u, x, hx => by
    simp only [bumpOffsets, List.mem_cons] at hx
    simp only [bumpUsed]
    have hmono : ∀ (ms : List Nat) (v : Nat), v ≤ bumpUsed ms v := by
      intro ms
      induction ms with
      | nil => intro v; exact Nat.le_refl v
      | cons m ms ih => intro v; simp only [bumpUsed]; have := ih (v + bumpTake m); omega
    rcases hx with rfl | hx
    · have := hmono ns (x + bumpTake n)
      omega
    · have := regions_in_arena ns (u + bumpTake n) x hx
      omega

-- § step rows

/-- The four step-state integers the host stages for `cell`. -/
def stepRow (cell : Nat) : List Nat := [cell, cell + 1, (cell + 1) / 4, cell + 1]

/-- The K/V count of a staged row is one past the cell: the new cell is attended to. -/
theorem stepRow_kv (cell : Nat) : (stepRow cell)[1]? = some (cell + 1) := rfl

/-- The pooled-block count is the K/V count divided by the 4-cell index block. -/
theorem stepRow_blocks (cell : Nat) : (stepRow cell)[2]? = some ((cell + 1) / 4) := rfl

/-- Catch-up rows (`t < T ≤ max_t`) never collide with chain rows (`max_t + j - 1`, `j ≥ 1`). -/
theorem catchup_below_chain (t T maxT j : Nat) (ht : t < T) (hT : T ≤ maxT) (hj : 1 ≤ j) :
    t < maxT + j - 1 := by
  omega

/-- Chain rows stay below the round's full row `2 * max_t - 1`. -/
theorem chain_below_full (maxT j : Nat) (hj : 1 ≤ j) (hj2 : j + 2 ≤ maxT) :
    maxT + j - 1 < 2 * maxT - 1 := by
  omega

/-- The full row fits the `2 * max_t` rows the mapped staging holds. -/
theorem full_row_fits (maxT : Nat) (h : 1 ≤ maxT) : 2 * maxT - 1 < 2 * maxT := by
  omega

-- § attention width and window

/-- The draft attention's selection width: window or context, rounded up to 64. -/
def capOf (cells : Nat) : Nat := (cells + 63) / 64 * 64

/-- The width covers every cell the layer may attend to. -/
theorem cap_covers (cells : Nat) : cells ≤ capOf cells := by
  unfold capOf; omega

/-- The width is a whole number of 64-cell tiles. -/
theorem cap_tiles (cells : Nat) : capOf cells % 64 = 0 := by
  unfold capOf; omega

/-- The effective window: the requested one if strictly inside the context, else 0 (every cell). -/
def windowOf (window maxCells : Nat) : Nat :=
  if 0 < window ∧ window < maxCells then window else 0

/-- An effective window is always smaller than the context. -/
theorem window_lt_context (w m : Nat) (hm : 0 < m) : windowOf w m < m := by
  unfold windowOf
  split <;> omega

/-- The attention width never exceeds the context's own width. -/
theorem cap_le_context_cap (w m : Nat) (hm : 0 < m) :
    capOf (if windowOf w m > 0 then windowOf w m else m) ≤ capOf m := by
  have hw := window_lt_context w m hm
  unfold capOf
  split <;> omega

-- § the draft chain

/-- Leading steps whose gate passed (`pj >= min_p`), stopping at the first failure. -/
def leading : List Bool → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | b :: bs => if b then 1 + leading bs else 0

/-- Drafts produced: the round's first plus the leading chain steps. -/
def chainLen (gates : List Bool) : Nat := 1 + leading gates

/-- The leading count never exceeds the number of chain steps. -/
theorem leading_le : ∀ bs : List Bool, leading bs ≤ bs.length

/-!
# MODULE: speculative_verify_window
SOURCES: src/core/verify.cpp
The verify window of speculative decoding: T tokens (the last accepted one plus drafts) run through all
48 layers in one captured graph, optionally split into two token groups A and B so the CPU computes one
group's experts while the GPU runs the other's mixer.  Each (layer, group) rings the doorbell with a
unique sequence number; the host serves the pool in that order.  After the window the argmax prefix
that agrees with the drafts is accepted and `commit` replays the state updates of the kept tokens.

## Source semantics
* Groups: `G = 2` iff split and `T ≥ 2`; A = [0, ⌈T/2⌉), B = [⌈T/2⌉, T); otherwise one group [0, T).
* Ring number of (layer l, group g) is `l*G + g + 1`; the host's k-th wait is `k + 1` with
  `l = k / G`, `g = k % G`, so host and graph agree on every ring.
* Accepted count `a`: the longest prefix with `window[i+1] = out[i]`; the round emits `a + 1 ≤ T` tokens.
* `commit` stages `[n_keep, n_keep-1, pos0, pos0+1, …, -1, …]`.
* Flag B only rises (`raise_flag` is a compare-exchange max).
* The GPU plan's u64 pointer block starts at an even i32 offset (8-byte aligned) and the plan's regions
  (counts, start, dst, tok, ptr, ptr2, start2) fit `plan_i32`.
* A window may not run past the context: `pos0 + T ≤ max_cells`.

## Form template identifiers
groupBegin/groupEnd ↔ tb_/te_ · ringOf ↔ `l * G + grp + 1` · acceptLen ↔ the `while (a < T-1 && …)` loop ·
commitRow ↔ h_commit_ · raise ↔ raise_flag · ptrOff/planI32 ↔ ptr_off / plan_i32_ · windowFits ↔ run guard
-/

namespace SpeculativeVerifyWindow

-- § token groups

/-- Number of groups for a window of `T` tokens. -/
def groups (split : Bool) (T : Nat) : Nat := if split = true ∧ 2 ≤ T then 2 else 1

/-- First token of group `g`. -/
def groupBegin (T g : Nat) : Nat := if g = 0 then 0 else (T + 1) / 2

/-- One past the last token of group `g`. -/
def groupEnd (G T g : Nat) : Nat := if g = 0 then (if G = 2 then (T + 1) / 2 else T) else T

/-- A split window's groups partition `[0, T)`: A starts at 0, B starts where A ends, B ends at T. -/
theorem split_partition (T : Nat) :
    groupBegin T 0 = 0 ∧ groupEnd 2 T 0 = groupBegin T 1 ∧ groupEnd 2 T 1 = T := by
  simp [groupBegin, groupEnd]

/-- Both groups of a split window are non-empty, so each rings. -/
theorem split_nonempty (T : Nat) (hT : 2 ≤ T) :
    groupBegin T 0 < groupEnd 2 T 0 ∧ groupBegin T 1 < groupEnd 2 T 1 := by
  simp only [groupBegin, groupEnd, if_true]
  simp
  omega

/-- An unsplit window is a single group covering every token. -/
theorem unsplit_whole (T : Nat) : groupBegin T 0 = 0 ∧ groupEnd 1 T 0 = T := by
  simp [groupBegin, groupEnd]

  simp [groups]

/-- The doorbell value the graph publishes for (layer, group). -/
def ringOf (G l g : Nat) : Nat := l * G + g + 1

/-- The host's k-th wait is exactly the graph's ring for (k / G, k % G). -/

  unfold ringOf
  have := Nat.div_add_mod k G
  rw [Nat.mul_comm] at this
  omega

theorem ring_increasing (G l g l' g' : Nat) (hg : g < G) (hg' : g' < G)
    (h : l < l' ∨ (l = l' ∧ g < g')) : ringOf G l g < ringOf G l' g' := by
  unfold ringOf
  rcases h with h | ⟨rfl, h⟩
  · have : (l + 1) * G ≤ l' * G := Nat.mul_le_mul_right G h
    rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul] at this
    omega
  · omega

  unfold ringOf
  have h1 : (L - 1) * G + G = L * G := by
    have : L - 1 + 1 = L := by omega
    calc (L - 1) * G + G = (L - 1 + 1) * G := by rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul]
      _ = L * G := by rw [this]
  omega

/-- Longest prefix of drafts confirmed by the window's argmax (`window[i+1] = out[i]`). -/
def acceptLen : List (Nat × Nat) → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | (d, o) :: ps => if d = o then 1 + acceptLen ps else 0

theorem accept_le : ∀ ps : List (Nat × Nat), acceptLen ps ≤ ps.length
  | [] => Nat.le_refl 0
  | (d, o) :: ps => by
    simp only [acceptLen, List.length_cons]
    have := accept_le ps
    split <;> omega

    acceptLen ps + 1 ≤ T := by
  have := accept_le ps
  omega

theorem round_emits (ps : List (Nat × Nat)) : 1 ≤ acceptLen ps + 1 := by
  omega

/-- A rejected first draft keeps exactly one token. -/
theorem reject_first (d o : Nat) (ps : List (Nat × Nat)) (h : d ≠ o) : acceptLen ((d, o) :: ps) = 0 := by
  simp [acceptLen, h]

/-- Entry `t` of the commit's position list: a kept position or `-1`. -/
def commitRow (pos0 : Int) (nKeep t : Nat) : Int := if t < nKeep then pos0 + t else -1

/-- Kept entries are consecutive positions from `pos0`. -/

    commitRow pos0 n (t + 1) = commitRow pos0 n t + 1 := by
  unfold commitRow
  have h1 : t + 1 < n := h
  have h2 : t < n := by omega
  simp only [h1, h2, if_true]
  push_cast
  omega

  unfold commitRow
  have : ¬ t < n := by omega
  simp [this]

/-- `raise_flag`: the compare-exchange loop leaves the larger of the current value and the new one. -/
def raise (cur v : Nat) : Nat := max cur v

/-- Flag B never decreases, so a late host function cannot undo a later layer's raise. -/
theorem raise_monotone (cur v : Nat) : cur ≤ raise cur v := by
  unfold raise; omega

/-- After a raise the flag satisfies the waiter for `v`. -/
theorem raise_reaches (cur v : Nat) : v ≤ raise cur v := by
  unfold raise; omega

/-- Raises commute: the order host functions complete in does not matter. -/
theorem raise_comm (cur a b : Nat) : raise (raise cur a) b = raise (raise cur b) a := by
  unfold raise; omega

/-- Offset of the u64 pointer block: the i32 header rounded up to even. -/
def ptrOff (cap : Nat) : Nat := (4 + (cap + 1) + cap + cap + 1) / 2 * 2

/-- Total i32 words of one plan slot. -/
def planI32 (cap : Nat) : Nat := ptrOff cap + 4 * cap + (cap + 1) + 1

  unfold ptrOff; omega

/-- The pointer block starts after counts, start, dst and tok. -/
theorem ptrOff_after_header (cap : Nat) : 4 + (cap + 1) + cap + cap ≤ ptrOff cap := by
  unfold ptrOff; omega

/-- `ptr` (cap u64) and `ptr2` (cap u64) end where `start2` begins, and `start2` (cap + 1) fits the slot. -/
theorem plan_regions_fit (cap : Nat) :
    ptrOff cap + 2 * cap + 2 * cap = ptrOff cap + 4 * cap ∧
      ptrOff cap + 4 * cap + (cap + 1) < planI32 cap := by
  unfold planI32; omega

/-- `run` refuses a window that would run past the context. -/
def windowFits (pos0 T maxCells : Nat) : Prop := pos0 + T ≤ maxCells

/-- Every position the window stages is a valid cell. -/
theorem window_cells_valid (pos0 T m t : Nat) (h : windowFits pos0 T m) (ht : t < T) : pos0 + t < m := by
  unfold windowFits at h; omega

end SpeculativeVerifyWindow
